title: Congruence of list search
statement: Let $\alpha$ be a type, let $xs$ be a finite list of elements of $\alpha$, and let $p,q : \alpha \to \{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$. If $p(a)=q(a)$ for every $a$ in $xs$, then searching $xs$ for the first element satisfying $p$ gives the same result as searching for the first element satisfying $q$.
hypotheses_covered: The predicates agree on every element of $xs$
